# YallaFlow 1.1.0

Connected Requirements and optional AI quality delivery. Every capability in this release is opt-in, and projects that do not use them see no change.

> You describe the intent. YallaFlow supplies the project.

## What's new

- **Work from your tracker.** Say "implement acme/shop#12" or "work on SHOP-42". The agent imports the GitHub Issue, Jira issue, or Azure DevOps work item as a preserved source: description, acceptance criteria, comments, attachments, and a link back to the ticket. The requirements it records trace to the ticket. By default, the agent fetches the ticket with the integration it already has, and YallaFlow stays offline. If it has none, `yallaflow intake ticket <ref> --fetch` fetches read-only, with a token from your environment that is never stored. Ticket text is treated as untrusted data, never as instructions to the agent.
- **AI QC with Playwright, when you ask.** The agent plans functional and exploratory scenarios from the acceptance criteria, runs them with the Playwright CLI or MCP, and records honest results. A scenario counts as passed only if it was actually executed, with evidence. Failures come with steps to reproduce them. Under the default advisory policy, failures are reported and never block completion. Under the strict policy, an explicit opt-in, they withhold *quality approval*, which stays separate from the task being done.
- **Smart demos, with optional video.** The agent proposes the few scenarios worth showing, in priority order, for a business or developer audience. You approve or change the scope before anything is recorded. Recordings and screenshots stay on your machine, and a demo is never presented as test evidence.
- **Local reports.** `.yallaflow/work/<id>/quality/report.md` and a standalone `report.html` link every video, screenshot, and trace. Media is hashed and excluded from Git by default. Nothing is uploaded.

Under the hood:

- Agent Contract v10.
- Skill Registry v9, with the on-demand skills `requirement-import`, `ai-qc`, and `smart-demo`. Every required workflow chain is unchanged.
- No schema changes, and still four runtime dependencies.

## Upgrade

```bash
npm install -g yallaflow@1.1.0
cd your-project
yallaflow agent refresh --dry-run
yallaflow agent refresh
```

Commit `.yallaflow/AGENT.md`. Only the YallaFlow-managed block changes. A 1.0.x CLI keeps reading projects that used the new capabilities and reports the newer contract without downgrading it.

## Limitations

- Tracker import is read-only and one ticket at a time: no sync, bulk import, or writeback. Live tracker calls are verified against recorded payloads and a local server, not the hosted services.
- YallaFlow does not drive the browser. QC and demo results are the agent's recorded claims, held to the honesty rules and hashed. Video needs Playwright's ffmpeg.
- Strict quality approval is a signal, not a lock.
- Unchanged from 1.0.x: Windows is not verified yet; no OCR; one moderate, mitigated dependency advisory (`file-type` via `officeparser`).
